title: Residue-field criterion for a map of finite locally free modules
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $v:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ be a morphism of finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-modules (that is, $S$ has an open cover on each member of which $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal F$ are locally free of some constant finite rank [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]). For $s\in S$, write $\mathcal E\otimes\kappa(s)$ for the fibre $\mathcal E_s\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\kappa(s)$, and similarly for $\mathcal F$. If for every point $s\in S$ the induced map $\mathcal E_s\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\kappa(s)\to\mathcal F_s\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\kappa(s)$ is an isomorphism, then $v$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix s∈S and put R=O_{S,s}, with maximal ideal m and residue field kappa(s). On an open neighbourhood of s both modules are free of finite rank [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], so E_s and F_s are finite free R-modules. Let C=coker(v_s), a finitely generated R-module (quotient of F_s). Right exactness of tensor product and surjectivity of the fibre map give C/mC=0, so C=0 by Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (with N=0); thus v_s is surjective. Since F_s is free, this surjection splits: E_s ≅ K ⊕ F_s with K=ker(v_s), so K is a direct summand of E_s, hence finitely generated, and the split exact sequence 0→K→E_s→F_s→0 stays exact after tensoring with kappa(s). Hence K⊗kappa(s) is the kernel of the fibre map E_s⊗kappa(s)→F_s⊗kappa(s), which is injective by hypothesis; so K/mK=0, and Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] gives K=0. Hence v_s is bijective.
